subject: Re: Data locality & deletion — BlueBridge DPA redline negotiation
messages:
From: Samantha Green <samantha.green@bluebridge.com>
To: alex_martinez@redwood.com
Cc: Marcus Liu <marcus.liu@bluebridge.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Aug 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Data locality + deletion questions for DPA redline

Hi Alex,

Thanks for taking this. Our legal and security teams spotted three areas in the draft DPA we sent over (attached as bluebridge-dpa-redlines.pdf) that need clarity before procurement can proceed:

1) Backups / disaster recovery: the redline asks that backups may be stored outside the primary geo for up to 180 days. We need a written operational justification and a rollback plan.
2) Certified deletion: counterparty wants a shorter certified-delete SLA for customer data (our suggested 30 days) and proof-of-deletion artifacts.
3) Legal hold carveouts: how will Redwood surface and preserve data when a lawful hold is triggered while meeting residency guarantees?

Can you propose a detailed operational playbook and a single consolidated redline we can put back into the doc? We are targeting a PO by 8/23, so time is tight.

Attachments: bluebridge-dpa-redlines.pdf (pdf)

Samantha
Samantha Green
Senior Counsel, BlueBridge Systems
From: alex_martinez@redwood.com
To: Samantha Green <samantha.green@bluebridge.com>
Cc: Marcus Liu <marcus.liu@bluebridge.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 15 Aug 2029 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data locality + deletion questions for DPA redline

Samantha —

Appreciate the clear ask. Short answers up front:
- Backups/DR: We can agree to a limited cross‑region backup retention for encrypted snapshots strictly for disaster recovery, with admin‑initiated restores only and audit trail. Proposed maximum hold: 90 days (we can discuss 180 if required for regulation, but need tighter controls).
- Certified deletion: Redwood can provide a certified deletion manifest within 10 business days of request for primary data; for backups the manifest will indicate snapshot destruction schedule and keys revoked.
- Legal hold: We will implement a scoped hold workflow that records the hold token, suspends deletion, and logs access; holds are visible to customer admins via the Console and via the shared evidence folder in Drive.

I attached our initial proposal (redwood-dpa-proposal-v1.pdf) and a short operational playbook stub (erase-playbook.md) that maps requests to actions. Can we jump on a 30 min call tomorrow to walk BlueBridge legal through the operational controls?

Next steps I propose:
- Agree on a backup hold limit (30 / 90 / 180)
- Confirm certified-delete SLA and sample manifest fields
- Define legal-hold visibility and timeline for release

If you want, I can include Laura on the call to confirm commercial tradeoffs and Ben for any engineering implementation questions.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Account Exec — Redwood Inference
From: alex_martinez@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 15 Aug 2029 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: Data locality + deletion questions for DPA redline — need guidance

Laura / Ben —

Looping you both in. BlueBridge pushed back on 180-day cross-geo backups and wants a 30-day certified-delete SLA. They need operational proof artifacts in Drive and a clear legal-hold playbook. Timebox: they want PO by 8/23.

Options I see:
- Commercial compromise: 90-day encrypted snapshot hold for DR only + certified-delete manifest within 10 business days; offer a one-time onboarding exception to 180 days only if regulator mandates (requires AE escalation).
- Operational controls: restrict cross-geo backups to encrypted snapshots stored with keys in US KMS, admin-initiated restores only, automated tombstone + key-rotation schedule. Provide deletion manifest with snapshot IDs, deletion timestamps, and KMS key rotation logs.

Questions:
1) Is 90 days an acceptable standard concession for enterprise?
2) Do we have a documented template manifest (fields) we can share with them now?

Attaching redwood-dpa-proposal-v1.pdf and erase-playbook.md (stubs).

—Alex
From: Samantha Green <samantha.green@bluebridge.com>
To: alex_martinez@redwood.com
Cc: Marcus Liu <marcus.liu@bluebridge.com>, legal@bluebridge.com
Date: Fri, 16 Aug 2029 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data locality + deletion questions for DPA redline

Alex —

Thanks for the fast reply. We did an internal review. BlueBridge legal will not accept 180 days outside the primary geo without escrow or additional controls. Our asks:

- Primary request: keep backups within the customer’s residency geo. If cross-geo is unavoidable, cap at 30 days and require immediate notification to BlueBridge security, plus the deletion manifest at time of snapshot destruction.
- Certified deletion SLA: 30 days for primary + backups where feasible; if longer (e.g., 90 days) we need a defined SLA credit and an explicit onshore-restore-only clause.
- Legal hold: while a hold is active we need read-only evidence access; we will accept a hold token with machine-readable metadata if the Console shows hold state and we can export the hold report.

Also: can you produce a sample deletion manifest we can review? The Drive link you suggested would be ideal for artifacts.

We’re not trying to be obstinate — this is a regulated workload and our infosec has a hard remit. If you can give us a narrowly scoped, auditable compromise by EOD Monday (8/19) we should be good to hit procurement.

Samantha
From: alex_martinez@redwood.com
To: Samantha Green <samantha.green@bluebridge.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 19 Aug 2029 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data locality + deletion questions for DPA redline

Samantha —

Proposed compromise below, aiming to be prescriptive so legal can redline:

1) Backups/DR: Cross‑geo encrypted snapshots are permissible only when primary region capacity or regulatory requirements dictate. Standard offer: 90 days max cross‑geo hold for encrypted snapshots (AES‑GCM). For customers requiring strict onshore residency we can commit to 30 days, but that will incur an onboarding engineering validation and a one‑time migration fee. Restore process: account admin must request restore via Console; all restores are logged and require two‑party approval (account admin + Redwood ops).

2) Certified deletion: For primary customer data we will provide a certified deletion manifest within 10 business days of request. Manifest fields: snapshot ID, object keys, deletion timestamp (UTC), KMS key rotation identifier, operator ID, and audit hash. For backups: manifest will include scheduled destruction date and proof of KMS key revocation once completed.

3) Legal hold: Holds are represented by a unique hold token in the Console and are visible to customer admins. While a hold is active, scheduled deletions are suspended, but data remains encrypted and access is restricted to named hold-stewards. Hold reports can be exported as CSV or PDF to the shared Drive folder.

Operational evidence and sample manifest uploaded to Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cBlueBridgeDPA. I attached erase-playbook.md for the workflow. If BlueBridge accepts 90 days as a default with an explicit onshore-path for customers that need 30, we can move forward this week.

If you prefer a bilateral escrow for 180 days we need to escalate to VP Legal — that will likely push the schedule beyond 8/23.

Would you like me to convert the above into a single paragraph redline for your counsel?

Thanks,
Alex
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: alex_martinez@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 20 Aug 2029 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: BlueBridge DPA — recommendation

Alex / Ben — quick internal note:

- Approve offering 90-day cross-geo backup hold as standard, with documented one-time exception path to 30 days onshore for regulated customers (requires migration fee).
- Ben: confirm we can produce manifests with fields Alex listed within 10 business days (engineering needs to confirm extraction + signing process).
- I'll prepare the commercial language: automatic SLA credit (0.5% TCV) if deletion timelines are missed more than once in a rolling 12 months.

I'll join the call with BlueBridge if Alex wants a commercial handoff.

Laura Bennett
Sales Director, Redwood Inference
